support_summary: D5/D6/D1: two researchers both prompted ChatGPT and independently validated citations with disagreements resolved by consensus but no agreement figure reported (Methods); topics author-chosen with list in Multimedia Appendix 1; verification across Google Scholar, PubMed, Google Search and DOI Foundation (Table 2). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D7 settled low; D8 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1: 120 questions author-developed across 8 radiology subspecialties with no external sampling frame (Methods; Supplementary Material 1); all other domains low - verbatim prompt presented December 2024 with default parameters, Radiologist 1 blinded and did not pose the questions, RAS 0=fabricated defined against Medline/Google Scholar/DOAJ/web searches (Table 2). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled some concerns; Overall settled some concerns. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D5/D6/D3: paper never states who verified the 176 citations or whether verification was duplicated or blinded, and no generation settings are reported (Methods; Table 1); verification source itself was strong and sequential (Google Scholar, then author-list and title searches, plus Scopus/PubMed/WorldCat), but DOI denominator differs between Table 1 (51/135) and Results text (51/141). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled low; D3 settled some concerns. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D2: Bard, Perplexity, SciSpace, Elicit and Bing are named with no version strings and no generation date is stated, so the run cannot be placed in time (Methods); verifier identity and duplicate verification are never reported, and no whole-reference fabricated count is printed - only RHS identifier errors against PubMed/Google Scholar (Tables 2-3). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23: no assessor disagreements on this study; judgements carried over unchanged.]

D1/D2/D3: topics were 50 ChatGPT-suggested proposals screened by five reviewers against FINER criteria, model is named only as ChatGPT (GPT-3) with no generation date, and no generation settings are reported; verification was strong - five researchers independently checked Scopus/PubMed/Google search, discrepancies discussed and resolved, Fleiss kappa 0.959 (Results; Table 3). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled some concerns; D2 settled some concerns; D3 settled no information; D7 settled low; D8 settled low; Overall settled some concerns. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D4/D7: verification was against PubMed alone, so references outside PubMed could be missed, and 'Non-Correct Citations' fold unrelated real references in with unfindable ones without a split (Summary; Table 1); duplicate verification itself was sound - two ophthalmology experts independently validated citations in phase 2 with Cohen kappa 0.74. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D6 settled low; D7 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D5/D6/D3: paper never states who verified the 59 references, whether verification was duplicated or blinded, or any generation settings (Methods; Results); topics were 20 author-chosen medical questions, and only 11 of 18 real references were journal articles, leaving handling of the other real references unclear, though existence was checked on PubMed and journal websites. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D4 settled low; D5 settled no information; D7 settled low; D8 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1/D8: prompts ran for 19 professors from the university hospital homepage but only the 8 professors ChatGPT recognised contributed the 260 references, and results are printed as percentages only with no counts (Main text; Table 1); prompt is printed verbatim with run dates 16-25 October 2023 and checking was by two observers against PubMed/Web of Science/Google Scholar/Lattes with consensus categorisation. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D2 settled some concerns; D7 settled some concerns. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D5/D6: paper never states who verified references or whether verification was duplicated or blinded - the reported Fleiss kappa measures consistency of chatbot answers across the 3 sessions, not verifier agreement (Table 4; Table 2 testing schedule); topics derived from papers with at least 100 citations lean to established guideline areas, while prompt text and per-arm testing dates are printed. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled some concerns; D2 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D4/D5/D6: no verification source is named anywhere and verifier identity, independence and duplication are all unreported, so fabrication calls (complete vs partial, Methods; Tables 4-5) cannot be checked against a stated source; topics were the full 192-question OrthoBullets SAE set, and video items were excluded because of Copilot limitations. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled low; D8 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1: two prompt versions were tested for each request and 'the query that led to the largest number of results was retained', i.e. the prompt was selected after seeing outputs (Methods); verifier identity and duplicate verification for the LLM-supplied papers are not reported (the two independent reviewers screened the PubMed systematic-review search only), and 'hallucinated' was defined as any 2 of title, first author or year wrong (Abstract; Table 2). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled some concerns; D2 settled some concerns; D3 settled high; D4 settled some concerns; D8 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D6: citation validity 'was assessed by a single evaluator' with specialty training and the authors state no inter-rater reliability testing was conducted (Results, citation hallucination assessment; Limitations); verification sources were strong (PubMed, Google Scholar, Web of Science, publisher databases, doi.org) across the full 331-question AAP examination set, but the Results text mislabels the GPT-5.0 IQ arm as 'GPT-4.0 IQ' (Table 5). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D2: DeepSeek is named with no version and no generation date is stated for either model (Table 3; section 3.5); a single conjunctivitis topic was used, verifier identity and duplication are unreported, and further errors (incomplete author lists, wrong issue/volume numbers) are described in text without counts, so partial matches are not counted apart. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled some concerns; D7 settled some concerns; D8 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D2/D5/D6: no model versions are stated for ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity (data collected 1-30 September 2025 on free-tier web interfaces, Methods) and all RHS scoring was by a single investigator, mitigated by a predefined rubric, a standardised PubMed/Google Scholar workflow and 95% intra-rater agreement on a random 200-reference re-check (Supplementary Material); no fabricated or accurate counts are printed, only RHS means (Tables 2-4). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D8 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D5/D6/D8: verification was programmatic against Crossref and PubMed APIs with printed verified/warning/failed/corrupted categories (Table 3), but there was no independent human duplicate check, three arms used unreported system-default models, the authors' own AI Research Army system is one of the arms under test, and several printed hallucination rates do not equal (failed+corrupted)/total from the printed counts (section 3.4). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23: no assessor disagreements on this study; judgements carried over unchanged.]

D2: model is named only as 'ChatGPT (free version)' with no version string and no generation date, and generation settings are never reported (temperature is raised only as a limitation); questions came from the Japanese Physical Therapy Guidelines (5 per section x 3 sections), references were checked by PMID/DOI then title searches on an unnamed database, with two assessors per section and weighted kappa 0.93-0.98 for reference accuracy, though section denominators sum to 38 against a text total of 37 (Table 2). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D2 settled some concerns; D3 settled no information; D4 settled low; D7 settled low; Overall settled some concerns. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1/D4: the 15 topic categories were themselves model-generated rather than drawn from an external frame, and bibliographic score 0 folds non-PubMed-indexed real sources (books/guidelines) in with nonexistent references, although any accessible academic database could also be checked (Methods, Reference assessment; Scoring system); verification was otherwise strong - two independent reviewers, Cohen kappa 0.966, consensus, single session March 2026 with web search enabled. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D2 settled low; D3 settled low; D5 settled some concerns. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1/D7/D4: three ad-hoc topics were probed in interactive conversations in which the model was confronted and re-prompted after its answers were seen, including a request for literature by co-author A. Kleyer (Main text; Figure 1); no verification source is named ('independent literature search' only - PubMed/Scopus/Web of Science appear only inside the quoted AI reply), model version is not stated, and no rule for partially matching references is given, with verifiers being the two authors who ran the chats. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D2 settled some concerns; D8 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D5/D6: paper never states who verified references or whether verification was duplicated or blinded - the reported Fleiss kappa measures consistency across the 3 chatbot sessions, not verifier agreement (Methods; Results Table 2); topics came from papers with at least 100 citations (established lean), prompt text is printed verbatim, sessions ran 8-10 July 2024 with a new conversation per question, and verification used PubMed, Web of Science and Google Scholar with six accuracy categories counted apart. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled some concerns; D2 settled some concerns. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D7/D8: references were classified as verifiable, inaccurate or hallucinated under a stated rule (Methods 3.3) but per-model hallucinated counts are not printed - only per-question hallucination-rate ranges - and inaccurate counts are not given apart per model (Results 4.1); sampling was systematic (first 200 Quora rosacea questions screened by predefined criteria), models are exactly versioned with web search disabled and default configuration, and the evaluating dermatologist was blinded to model identity. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D2 settled low; D6 settled high; D8 settled some concerns; Overall settled high. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D5/D7: references were cross-checked independently by two reviewers on PubMed, Google Scholar and Web of Science with discrepancies resolved by discussion but no agreement statistic, and author contributions show one verifier (DS) also generated the prompts and collected the data (Methods, Reference verification; Table 6); 'False' (n=61) folds fabricated and unverifiable references together with irrelevant real ones, with no split printed. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled some concerns; D6 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D4: fabrication was defined to include 'studies not indexed in PubMed', so verification on PubMed alone builds a coverage gap into the fabricated count itself (Results; Appendix C Table 4); each of the 5 graders also evaluated only citations from responses they themselves generated (single grader per response, element-by-element PubMed match, any discrepancy including minor typographical errors counted equally), though topics were all 70 AAOS CPG recommendations, prompts are in Appendix A, and runs were February-March 2026 on paid ChatGPT-5 with web search available under default settings. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D2 settled low; D7 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D6/D8: all references were independently evaluated by 2 investigators with discrepancies resolved by consensus but, as the authors note, no inter-rater reliability statistic was calculated, and counts are pooled across the 3 prompt types with per-prompt-group results printed only as mean accuracy scores (Table 1 vs Table 3); fabricated was defined as not found in PubMed, Google Scholar or CrossRef, with 0/1/2 accuracy counts printed per model (Tables 3-4). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D3 settled some concerns; D8 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1: the 10 neurocritical care topics were 'selected by a single domain expert without a formal consensus or Delphi process' and not stratified by evidence density (authors' Limitations); every other domain is low - identical zero-shot prompts on 10 March 2026 via official paid interfaces with retrieval disabled, and two blinded neurocritical care experts independently verified each reference against PubMed, DOI resolver, Google Scholar and CrossRef with Cohen kappa 0.91 and a stated 0-3 Hallucination Scale (Methods; Table 1). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D2 settled some concerns. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D6/D1: reference validation was by a single reviewer with, as the authors state, no inter-rater reliability data, using judgement-based classes (fabricated, misrepresented, accurate/supportive) whose fabricated and misrepresented counts are not printed separately - only the combined 29/88 hallucination count (Table 1; Results, Reference reliability); validation covered a correctness-stratified subsample (all 44 incorrect answers plus 44 randomly selected correct answers) of the 203 OITE questions, with GPT-5 run 29-30 August 2025 at default temperature 1.0 in a new chat per question and checked on PubMed, Google Scholar, Google and librarian-assisted searches. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled low; D6 settled high; D8 settled low; Overall settled high. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]
